NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE-1 ZONING MAP AMENDMENT AT
3127-3139 N. HALSTED ST. / 749-759 W. BRIAR PL.

The Applicant requests a zoning change for the property located at 3127-3139 North Halsted Street/749-
759 West Briar Place (the “Property”) from the B3-2 Community Shopping District to B2-5
Neighborhood Mixed-Use District in order to construct a 3-story addition to the existing 2-story building
and to construct a new 5-story addition resulting in a 5-story, 65 foot, 1 % inch tall mixed-use building
(the “Project”). The Project consists of sixty-six (66) residential dwelling units on the ground floor
through the Sth floor and approximately 1,233 square feet of commercial space on the ground floor.
There will be fourteen (14) vehicle parking spaces on the ground floor and 66 bicycle parking spaces.
The Project is approximately 1,195 feet from the Belmont CTA train stop and 180 feet from the Clark
Street CTA bus line. Accordingly, the Property is a Transit Served Location and eligible for a reduction
of the applicable parking requirement of fifty (50%) of the unit count, or thirty-three (33) parking
spaces.

The proposed Project also requires the following zoning relief in accordance with the review and
approval procedures set forth in Section 17-13-0303-D of the Zoning Ordinance:

“An administrative adjustment for the reduction of the required parking count from thirty-three
(33) parking spaces to fourteen (14) parking spaces (Section 17-13-1003-EE); and

(2) A variation to reduce the rear setback from the required combined 30.0 feet to 0.0 feet (Section
17-13-1101-B); and

&) A variation to eliminate the required loading berth (Section 17-13-1101-D); and

A variation to reduce the setback for stairway and elevator enclosures and elevator equipment

penthouses between side building lines from 69.1 feet to 33’- 4 4” (Section 17-13-1101-B); and

‘) All relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for the attached Plans.

Section 17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations.

(1) The Project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B of the Zoning
Ordinance such that the Project (i) is located within 1,320 feet from a CTA bus line corridor and
2,640 feet from a CTA rail station, (ii) is located in a B zoning district, and (iii) proposes at least
1:1 bicycle parking. The project will not have parking spaces in excess of 50% of the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for the subject zoning district.

(2) The Project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504 of the Zoning
Ordinance as follows: *

{i) the Project is subject to Section 17-3-0308 and therefore is subject to Section 17-3-
0504 ($17-3-0504-A);

(ii) the building is located within 5.0 feet of the sidewalk on both the North Halsted Street
and West Briar Place frontages ($17-3-0504-B);

(iii) the land use for the Project is designated in a non-commercial use group such that
Paragraph C is not applicable ($17-3-0504-C);

(iv) the primary entrance to the Project is on North Halsted Street. The Project does not
abut a pedestrian street ($17-3-0504-D);

(v) _ the Project is not a nonresidential use such that Paragraph E is not applicable ($17-3-
0504-E);

(vi) all off-street vehicle parking at the Project is located in an enclosed parking garage
(§$17-3-0504-F);

(vii) vehicle access to the enclosed parking garage is from the alley east of North Halsted
Street ($17-3-0504-G);

(viit) the Project is not located along a pedestrian street such that Paragraph H is not
applicable ($17-3-0504-H);

(ix) the Project is a residential use such that Paragraph I is not applicable ($17-3-0504-1;
and

(x) _ the encouraged uses set forth in Paragraph J are noted. The proposed use of the
ground floor commercial space is to be determined ($17-3-0504-I).

(3) The Project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide:
Station Area Typology for a “Major Activity Center”, which encourages higher density
residential uses near such rail stations with integrated retail.

(4) The Project will not have a number of parking space in excess of 50% of the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for the B zoning district.

(5) The Project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation (“CDOT”), and will be reviewed by CDOT in accordance with
that Plan.
